Introduction to Mental Health Nursing

What mental health is, what mental illness is, the historical background and the scope of mental health nursing.

🎯 After this chapter you can

  • Define mental health and mental illness
  • List the signs of positive mental health
  • Describe the history of psychiatric nursing in India
  • Explain the scope of mental health nursing

In simple words

Mental health is not just the absence of mental illness. It is a state of balance in which a person can use his abilities, cope with normal stresses, work productively and contribute to the community.

Mental illness is a disturbance of thinking, feeling, behaviour or perception that causes distress and interferes with daily life.

Signs of positive mental health

  • Accepts self, has realistic self-respect
  • Forms warm and satisfying relationships
  • Can work, play and be productive
  • Copies with stress and frustration
  • Feels secure and accepted
  • Can make decisions and take responsibility

A brief history of psychiatric nursing in India

  • 1745 to 1800 — lunatic asylums with custodial care (London, Bombay, Calcutta)
  • 1794 to 1858 — moral treatment began; restraint reduced
  • 1858 onwards — Lunacy Acts; Indian Lunacy Act 1912
  • 1947 — Indian Psychiatric Society formed
  • 1987 — Mental Health Act 1987
  • 2017 — Mental Healthcare Act 2017 — right to mental health care
  • Nurses — trained psychiatric nursing introduced in 1950s; MSc Nursing in psychiatry

Scope of mental health nursing

  • Assess and monitor mental status and risk
  • Give medicines and watch side effects
  • Provide physical care, nutrition and hygiene
  • Therapeutic communication and relationship building
  • Counsel and teach the patient and family
  • Crisis intervention and suicide prevention
  • Rehabilitation and community integration
  • Reduce stigma through education

🔴 Mental illness is not madness

Mental illness is a health problem, like diabetes or asthma. It is treatable, and most people recover and lead useful lives. Reject labels such as mad, possessed or dangerous.

🔴 Most important for exams

  1. Mental health = balance to use abilities, cope with stress and contribute to society.
  2. Mental illness = disturbance of thought, feeling or behaviour causing distress.
  3. Mental Healthcare Act 2017 replaced the 1987 Act.
  4. SCIMH = State Centre for Mental Health Sciences.
  5. DMHP = District Mental Health Programme.

⭐ Important for exams

  1. Mental hygiene = keeping the mind healthy; mental health nursing = promoting and restoring that health.
  2. Levels of prevention: promotion, early detection, treatment, rehabilitation.
  3. Nurses spend the most time with patients, so observation is the key skill.
  4. Stigma is reduced by education and community integration.
  5. National Mental Health Programme 1982; DMHP since 1996.

📌 Memory trick

Four levels = P-P-T-R: Promotion, Prevention, Treatment, Rehabilitation.

60-second revision

  • Mental health = balance for productive living; illness = distressing disturbance.
  • Signs of health: self-acceptance, relationships, work, coping.
  • History: asylums → moral treatment → MHA 1987 → MHCA 2017.
  • Nurse’s work: observe, medicate, comfort, counsel, rehabilitate.
  • NMHP + DMHP take mental health to the community.

Test yourself

Mental health is best defined as:

Answer: B. Mental health is a balance in which the person uses abilities, copes with stress, works and contributes to society.

The Mental Healthcare Act was passed in:

Answer: C. The Mental Healthcare Act 2017 replaced the Mental Health Act 1987 and guarantees access to mental health care.

Which is a sign of positive mental health?

Answer: B. Forming warm and satisfying relationships, self-acceptance and productivity are signs of positive mental health.

The District Mental Health Programme aims to:

Answer: B. DMHP provides accessible mental health care in the district and community, following the NMHP.

The nurse’s key skill in psychiatric nursing is:

Answer: B. Because nurses spend the most time with patients, observation and therapeutic communication are the key skills.
